lastCompletedStory.title: Append a cycle-metrics row on main, in place

nextStoryContext: US-003 added src/commands/cycle-metrics.ts: upsertCycleMetricsRowOnMain(cwd, eventLogJsonl, cycleId, spawnFn), the on-main writer for scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl. Contract for the US-004 caller (the loop's cycle-close step): call it once per closed cycle with the FULL current event-log content (.claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl) and the cycleId of the marker that just closed. Result union: `{ ok: true, committed: true, cycleId, bootstrapped, sha }` on success (bootstrapped=true means this write created the file for the first time via a full aggregateCycleMetrics derivation, matching --rebuild byte-for-byte); `{ ok: true, committed: false, reason: 'no-established-row', cycleId }` when the cycleId's marker has no left bound yet (e.g. it is the log's very first marker) -- a documented no-op, never a fabricated row; `{ ok: false, reason: 'diverged'|'detached-head'|'missing-main' }` (guard failure, passthrough from checkMainUpToDate) or `{ ok: false, reason: 'commit-failed', error }` (commitTreeToMain threw, e.g. CAS exhaustion -- caught, never propagated). US-004 should warn-and-continue on any `ok:false` result rather than crash the cycle. The store is read via `git show main:scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl` (readCycleMetricsContentFromMain, exported) and written through the SHARED src/git/on-main.ts plumbing (commitTreeToMain's FileWritesFn per-attempt-recompute form, checkMainUpToDate, pushMainBestEffort) -- no private byte-copy. In-place upsert (non-bootstrap path) replaces ONLY the matching cycleId's line, preserving every other line (including blank/malformed lines) byte-for-byte, mirroring appendOutcomeToLine (src/commands/pattern-records.ts). US-002's runStatsCycles/--rebuild path in src/commands/stats.ts is UNCHANGED by this story and remains the last sanctioned bulk-rewriter of the artifact on a feature branch (CAM-121 branch-clobber scar) -- from here on, only upsertCycleMetricsRowOnMain should write new rows on main.
